result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both give the same usable three-question test and put the log, camera list and counting method in the handout. B is stronger on the plant-manager audience: it leads with the decision, ends with an explicit approve/owner/deadline ask, and anticipates their likely questions. It also flags that 'most' in the 2–4 pm window has no supporting count rather than letting it stand. A is solid and compact, but it treats the managers' decision only lightly, mainly as an optional action sheet in the handout. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give the same three-question test and put the full log, the camera-angle list and the counting method in the handout. A is stronger on the plant-manager audience: it ends on an explicit ask slide (who approves, who owns each fix, by when) and warns not to write "most" without the actual 2–4 pm count. B's main audience step is suggesting owners and dates for the handout, and it adds unsupported touches like saying the scattered incidents had "no pattern worth acting on" and suggesting a by-week backup chart.
